source_request_policy.global_opt_in: EXTERNAL_REQUESTS_ENABLED defaults to false and gates all external polling, chart retrieval, Jev calls, and operator retry.
source_request_policy.source_allowlist: EXTERNAL_SOURCE_COLLECTORS defaults to empty. When global opt-in is true, only listed real collectors can poll; yahoo_quote and yahoo_chart are separate allowlist entries.
source_request_policy.jev_forwarding: TYPESAFE_ALLOWED_COLLECTORS is intersected with EXTERNAL_SOURCE_COLLECTORS. Jev may receive a source item only when its collector is explicitly admitted by both lists, a non-empty key is configured, and both finite daily budgets are positive. The effective set gates startup and scheduled drains, new ingestion, and operator retry.
source_request_policy.verification: The fresh-process offline verifier proves the saved-data default makes zero external fetch attempts. It launches one isolated process per collector with only that collector allowlisted, checks the expected request URL shape and exact health/delivery gates, and intercepts every external global fetch before network access. A separate mismatch case supplies an API key, positive finite budgets, and a Jev allowlist that does not intersect the active source allowlist; Jev health must remain disabled.

current_followup.result: The SEC's current Webmaster FAQ says EDGAR public filing content is free to access and reuse, and its Website Dissemination policy says sec.gov information may be copied or further distributed without SEC permission. This supports a narrow evaluation path using public EDGAR filing content. It is not blanket rights clearance for non-EDGAR publisher text, an SEC endorsement, or authorization to use a TypeSafe account.
sec_conditions: For the initial path, use public EDGAR filing content only; omit SEC marks/artwork and avoid any clearly third-party material embedded in a filing.
Configure a descriptive SEC User-Agent that identifies the operator and includes contact information; the SEC says automated tools must be classified.
Stay at or below the SEC limit of 10 requests per second aggregated across machines; the app's 125ms per-process start spacing is below this limit, but multiple processes are not coordinated.

Use a TypeSafe account authorized by its owner and confirm the current agreement, account limits, auto-refill, retention, telemetry, rejected-request billing, and that the intended product use fits the similar/competing-product restriction before dispatch.
current_followup.type_safe_billing: The MCA currently posted as last updated 2026-09-23 says credits are consumed by each submitted Input, and account settings control consumption/refills. The reviewed API documentation describes 429 and 529 retry behavior but does not say those submissions are free. Treat them as potentially billable until the authorized account owner verifies the account's actual billing behavior.
current_followup.type_safe_data_use: The current MCA grants TypeSafe processing of Input to provide the service and broad, perpetual processing of Customer Data to derive Telemetry; Telemetry includes hashes, summary statistics, classifications, metrics, and learnings, and may be used without restriction to improve TypeSafe products. The privacy policy says Inputs are not used to train or fine-tune models, but it also describes service-improvement and reasonably-necessary retention and says services are hosted in the U.S. The MCA also restricts use of Services or Output to develop a similar or competing product/service; the account owner should confirm that the intended Sentiment Desk use is within the account's permitted scope. These account-level terms must be reviewed separately from the SEC's public reuse policy.

findings.evidence: The MCA was last updated 2026-09-23. It places responsibility for input rights on the customer; credits are consumed by each submitted Input and auto-refill depends on account settings. Its telemetry definition includes hashes, summary statistics, classifications, metrics, and learnings, which may be processed without restriction to improve TypeSafe services. The privacy policy disclaims training/fine-tuning on Inputs and describes reasonably-necessary retention and U.S. hosting. Its poller and adapter now pace requests and stop/persist cooldown after HTTP 429, as covered by mocked tests.

known_gaps: Raw upstream bodies are not retained. Delivery digests cover normalized parsed items and cannot prove parser correctness or replay raw bytes; Jev replay uses normalized observation fields.

Delivery state and newest collected-item event time are separate. An old source timestamp can coexist with a current successful delivery; source age is shown, but no universal content-staleness TTL is claimed because quiet periods and provider query semantics differ.

Yahoo quote retrieval time and source regularMarketTime are separate. A failed per-symbol refresh marks the retained quote as cached and exposes its original retrieval age. Market-closure and holiday correctness is not established by the app weekday/session display.

2026-09-28 exact-source chart verification passed: only provider-timestamped points in the selected window are drawn; a real latest point outside the window is preserved as metadata and not repeated into generated display buckets.

GDELT is currently rate-limited with HTTP 429. Non-JSON bodies are rejected by the adapter and verified by tests; a post-fix live HTTP-200 non-JSON body was not observed. This is a coverage limitation, not evidence of no activity.

Source collectors retry on the next scheduled poll. Jev retries only explicit retryable HTTP 429 or documented HTTP 529 rejections through persisted, bounded scheduling (maximum three attempts), honoring valid Retry-After values and otherwise exponential backoff. Transport failures, generic server errors, malformed output, and model mismatches are not automatically resubmitted. A submitted failure requires provider-usage review and explicit operator confirmation before manual retry; corrupt judgments cannot be retried. Provider coverage and pagination completeness are not proven exhaustive.

No rights-reviewed public-source-to-Jev classifier evaluation, labeled real-source accuracy/calibration assessment, exhaustive source-coverage audit, or historical TypeSafe usage reconciliation has been completed.

The offline classifier evaluator consumes caller-prepared local JSON. It records the exact analyzed run digest but cannot authenticate TypeSafe receipts or independently verify reported scores/token counts; passing metrics require separate auditable provider evidence.

Provider pacing and cooldowns reduce this application's request bursts but do not verify current provider quotas, contract permissions, or behavior across multiple independent application processes. Exact provider terms and project-specific rights remain open.
